package_info.package_versions: Adobe Commerce 2.4.7 and earlier, Adobe Commerce Extended Support 2.4.3-ext-7 and earlier, Magento Open Source 2.4.7 and earlier, Adobe Commerce Webhooks Plugin 1.2.0 to 1.4.0
package_info.why_malicious: The affected package versions contain a critical information disclosure vulnerability (CVE-2024-34102) that, when chained with a glibc iconv flaw (CVE-2024-2961), allows remote code execution. Attackers exploit these flaws to inject payment skimmers, steal cryptographic keys, and exfiltrate sensitive customer and payment data, making the entire package version set highly susceptible to compromise and malicious activity.

execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in order checkout webpage (frontend template or loaded via compromised admin panel)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the checkout form submission, collects credit card data from input fields, and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to a remote attacker-controlled domain, resulting in payment data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating payment data from checkout forms to external domains is a classic sign of a web skimmer/magecart attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors, not arbitrary external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation or analytics scripts may read form fields, but should never send sensitive data to untrusted endpoints.
key_indicators: JavaScript event listeners on payment forms
Outbound network requests to non-payment domains
Collection of card number, expiry, and CVV

execution_context.file_location: Magento server filesystem (PHP file or shell command injection)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After remote code execution, the code reads the Magento cryptographic key from the configuration file and exfiltrates it via email to the attacker, enabling further compromise or decryption of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating cryptographic keys is a high-impact action that enables attackers to decrypt sensitive data or forge tokens.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Magento code should never transmit cryptographic keys outside the server or to untrusted parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup scripts may read config files, but should not email them to external addresses.
key_indicators: Reading env.php or other config files
Outbound email or network exfiltration of secrets

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2024-34102 (CosmicSting) to gain information disclosure and, when chained with CVE-2024-2961, achieve remote code execution on the Magento server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute arbitrary code on the server

attack_chain.action: Read and exfiltrate Magento cryptographic keys from server configuration files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains ability to decrypt sensitive data or further manipulate the store

attack_chain.action: Inject malicious JavaScript payment skimmer into checkout pages to steal customer credit card data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous exfiltration of payment data from customers

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected JavaScript event listeners on checkout/payment forms
Outbound network requests from frontend code to untrusted domains
Server-side access to /app/etc/env.php or other sensitive config files
Outbound email or HTTP requests containing cryptographic keys or sensitive data
file_indicators: Modified checkout templates or injected JavaScript in frontend files
New or modified PHP files with mail() or file_get_contents('/app/etc/env.php')
Unusual changes to /app/etc/env.php or related config files
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with payment processors
Connections to known skimmer C2 domains (e.g., malicious-skimmer.com)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to checkout page templates and injected JavaScript, especially code that collects and transmits payment data to external domains. Audit server logs for access to sensitive config files and outbound emails or HTTP requests containing cryptographic material. Use file integrity monitoring on key Magento files and network monitoring to detect suspicious exfiltration patterns.
